text:
Dear Principal [Name],

I am writing to support the proposed policy that would ban phones for the whole school day, including lunch. I know many students will oppose this idea. I understand why. But I believe a full-day ban would make our school a better place to learn and to be with each other.

**Lunch is when we connect with each other.**
Lunch is one of the few times in the day when we can talk freely with friends. Right now, many students spend that time looking down at their screens. Tables that could be loud with conversation are often quiet. Some students sit with a group but scroll alone. Without phones, students would have to talk, play games, or simply notice each other. That is how friendships form. It is also how lonely students get included.

**A class-only ban is hard to enforce.**
When phones are allowed at lunch, they come out the moment class ends. Students then carry that distraction back into the classroom. They want to finish a conversation or check a notification. Teachers spend time reminding students to put phones away. A single rule for the whole day is simpler. Everyone knows the expectation, and no one has to argue about when a phone is allowed.

**Phones fuel conflict during the day.**
Many arguments between students start or grow online. A message sent at lunch can turn into a fight by the end of the day. Photos and videos taken in the cafeteria can be shared without anyone's permission. A full-day ban would reduce these problems. It would give students a break from the pressure of social media for at least seven hours.

**Our minds need a real break.**
Research has linked heavy phone use to anxiety, poor sleep, and trouble focusing. Lunch should be a time to rest our minds. Scrolling does not give us that rest. A break without screens would help us return to afternoon classes calmer and more ready to learn.

**Addressing the concerns.**
Some parents worry about reaching their children in an emergency. This is a fair concern. The school office can handle urgent calls, as it did before phones were common. Students with medical needs could also receive exceptions. Other students may say they need phones to check schedules or homework. The school could provide this information on paper or on school computers.

I believe a full-day ban is a small sacrifice for a large benefit. It would help us focus, reduce conflict, and bring back real conversation at lunch. I hope you will adopt this policy.

Thank you for taking the time to consider my view.

Sincerely,
[Your Name]
[Grade]
